## Summary

A hook post, not a protocol: one claim, one effect list, one joke, one takeaway. The full text, in his order:

- **Hook:** "You know there's nothing stopping you from blasting stims and obscure Russian medicines to run laps around the competition, right?"
- **The claim:** "Bromantane being the best example of this - by increasing your dopamine production, life just becomes BETTER."
- **Effect list (his line breaks):** "Colours? Richer / Task initiation? Easier / Task completion? Seamless / Physical performance? Better / Physical resilience? Impressive"
- **Rhetorical Q&A:** "Is it that easy? Yeah, pretty much."
- **The rest, framed as optional:** "Whether you then want to be like me and stick on huge stacks of boner pills, Latvian heart medication, BPC157 & KPV to fix the gut, miscellaneous ancillaries and experimental compounds is up to you."
- **Takeaway and sign-off:** "Just get the basics right and nail the easy wins, you know? / The thoughts of the biohacker."

The joke line decodes against the 11-17 manifest: boner pills = tadalafil, Latvian heart medication = meldonium (Mildronat is the Latvian original), BPC-157 & KPV = the gut peptides. He is describing his own daily stack from [[2026-11-17-zygomatic03-daily-stack-t3-meldonium]] as optional extras around a bromantane core.

**The photo — the part that is actually new.** Nine items laid flat on a white marble-veined counter, no hands, no caption overlay:

- **A bromantane dropper bottle:** black glass, holographic silver label, lying on its side with the label's left edge out of frame. Readable: "…OMANTANE / 100 MG/ML / …0 ML / …USA.COM / …R HUMAN CONSUMPTION". That is **liquid bromantane at 100 mg/mL sold by a US research-chemical vendor — not a pharmacy pack.** The leading letters are outside the frame, so the substance is an inference from the suffix plus the strength.
- **BPC-157 + KPV bottle** (QTY 60; 500 mcg / 500 mcg), same holographic stock and the same "…USA.COM" / "…FOR HUMAN CONSUMPTION" label tail — looks like the same vendor as the bromantane (inference from label style).
- **NOW L-Tyrosine 750 mg "Extra Strength"** (Neurotransmitter Support, Pharmaceutical Grade, Healthy Glandular Function, Supports Mental Alertness; 90 capsules) and **NOW Choline & Inositol** (100 veg capsules) — both on the 11-17 manifest; this is the "Extra Strength" tyrosine bottle OCR'd there.
- **Mildronat (Grindeks) meldonium 500 mg**, 10-capsule blister, opened — about seven wells emptied (estimate).
- **Tadalafil 5 mg film-coated tablets** (Accord), pink carton.
- **Designs for Health Taurine + Glycine powder**, 250 g tub.
- **Two small dropper vials** with cream typed labels, headings read as "Kuinone" and "Tuinone" (spelling uncertain); the second's fine print is partly legible as "Thymoquinone (CAS …)" in "organic olive oil", the first is unidentified.

Provenance: the label text was read by one vision pass on the local jpg (each label cross-checked by it on zoom crops). WinRT OCR at native size confirms the tyrosine, meldonium and tadalafil items and catches "MG/ML" and "CONSUMPTION" fragments next to a garbled "…aNTRNE" that sits on the same label; rotated and upscaled re-OCR could not resolve the bromantane label itself (sideways text). Treat the bromantane read as high-confidence but single-pass, and the counts (nine items, seven of ten wells) as estimates.

## Why it matters

Fourth capture from this author and the thinnest as protocol — a re-promo of the article already in the vault, with no dose, no cycle length and no link beyond that article. What it adds is a change of framing plus one piece of physical evidence:

1. **Bromantane is now pitched as the 80/20.** The 10-26 article built a seven-compound replacement for Vyvanse with bromantane as its "highly logical fit for ADHD" core. Here the core is the whole pitch and everything else is explicitly optional ("is up to you"), under the banner "get the basics right and nail the easy wins". Two effect lines are new wording — task completion ("seamless") and "physical resilience"; the article had task initiation, endurance and "modest drive".
2. **The post drops the cons he published four days earlier.** [[2026-11-27-zygomatic03-favourite-drugs-pros-cons]] lists bromantane's downsides unprompted: best results come from cycling, and "not always easy to find a reputable source". Neither appears here. The photo answers the sourcing point in a way the text does not: the bottle on his counter is a research-chemical dropper carrying a not-for-human-consumption label tail and a vendor URL — not the 50 mg tablet regimen the article's "ran 50mg/day, 6-8 week courses" reads as (Ladasten, the Russian original, is a 50 mg tablet). A 100 mg/mL liquid also makes the dose a drop-count, and nothing on camera says how he measures it.
3. **The manifest widens again.** Against the 11-17 photo the new items are the taurine + glycine powder and the two "…inone" vials (one apparently thymoquinone, the black-seed-oil bioactive, in olive oil — fine print only partly legible). The stack keeps growing while the message says "just the basics".

Skepticism gates, unchanged and sharpened: n=1 self-report by a stack influencer whose article carries his own vendor code (flagged 11-10). Bromantane's evidence base is Russian-only, it is WADA-banned, and "colours become more vibrant" is his subjective dopamine tell, not an outcome. The photo is consistent with him taking the compound and inconsistent with assuming his source is a pharmacy: a research-chemical liquid is unverified for content and concentration regardless of who posts it. UAE posture unchanged from the earlier notes (not a registered medicine there; importing it is customs-seizure risk; armodafinil is prescription-controlled, tadalafil and T3 prescription-only). RD's stance since 11-10 is checking, not ordering, and this link arrived bare with no ask — **reference-only, no task filed**. If bromantane ever moves from curiosity to intent, the lane is the same as before: a doctor consult with bloodwork, not a vendor dropper bottle.
